title: FireSquire: Pre-Reboot Check
err: Could not run the check engine.
err_hint: Try again in a moment. If it keeps failing, the syslog may say why.
tools_lead: FireSquire checks whether your server will come back up clean before you reboot, and gives one verdict (All clear / Smouldering / The roof is on fire) with the exact findings. It is advisory only: it reads the host and reports. On the flash it writes an empty test file, to check that /boot is writable, and deletes it right away. It also keeps the CRC error count of every disk there, so it can tell when one rises.
tools_intro: It looks for the reboot landmines that are detectable from the running system:
tools_li: Array started & clean: every device assignment OK (no disabled/invalid/missing disk)
No parity/sync/rebuild/clear or mover in progress
No container mounting a host runtime dir, no stuck docker.img/libvirt.img loop
Flash writable, free space, recent crashes, running VMs, services, SMART health
Apps in your fortress: work a reboot would cut short, such as a running backup or update
ZFS pools and devices, btrfs device errors and rising CRC counts, each with the disk's port
Shutdown time-outs, an unclean last shutdown, files open over SMB and NFS, the UPS and the age of the flash backup
tools_note: Advisory only, apart from a write test and the CRC counts on the flash

io_ok: No disk/IO errors in syslog since boot.

fortress_busy_open: {0} on {1} is still busy with {2}. Let it finish before rebooting.
fortress_ok: {0} app(s) in your fortress answered. None is busy with work a reboot would cut short.
fortress_alone: No other app of your fortress is in reach right now.
fortress_skip: FireSquire could not reach the fortress and skipped its apps.
zfs_degraded: ZFS pool {0} is {1}. Fix it before rebooting.
zfs_dev_errors: ZFS pool {0}: {1} has {2} read, {3} write and {4} checksum errors.
zfs_ok: {0} ZFS pool(s) online, no device errors.

crc_rose: The CRC errors on {0} rose from {1} to {2} since the last check. Check or replace the cable on this port.
scrutiny_link: Scrutiny keeps the SMART history of your disks. Open it to see when the counts started to rise.
scrutiny_tip: Tip: Scrutiny from Community Apps keeps a SMART history of your disks, so you can see when a count started to rise.
smart_failing: SMART health FAILING on:{0}. Investigate before rebooting.
smart_none: No disks found for SMART check.
smart_skip: smartctl not found, skipped SMART check.
help_body: Bugs, ideas or wishes? You're welcome to open an issue on GitHub. Questions get answered in the support thread on the Unraid forum.
about_body: FireSquire is a free plugin for Unraid, built by one knight on evenings and weekends, with no accounts, no telemetry and no ads.
about_coin: If it has earned a place on your server, toss a coin to your knight: it helps cover the costs and keeps the project alive.
give_appeal: Toss a coin to your knight: it covers part of the costs and keeps the project alive. Everything I build costs nothing and shows no ads.
coffee_intro: The payment runs through Buy Me a Coffee. You do not need an account.
paypal_intro: The payment runs through PayPal, with your PayPal account or by card without one.
paypal_thanks: Thank you, your donation went through.
paypal_failed: PayPal cannot be reached right now. Try again later or pick another way to give.
crypto_intro: Pick a currency and a network, then scan the code or copy the address.
crypto_notag: No destination tag and no memo needed.
n_body_go: Nothing in the last check stands in the way of a reboot.
n_test_body: If you can read this, FireSquire's messages reach you.
n_lead: FireSquire sends its verdict when a check ends in "Smouldering" or "The roof is on fire", and once more when it is back to "All clear". A check without findings sends nothing.
n_nohelper: The notification helper is not installed yet, so FireSquire cannot send anything for now.
n_sent: The test is on its way.
n_f_headers: Headers, one per line as Name: value
n_sched_lead: FireSquire runs the check on its own, so the messages come without a click.
timeouts_ok: Unraid's shutdown time-out of {0}s covers containers and VMs ({1}s).
timeouts_short: Unraid waits {0}s for a clean shutdown, but containers ({1}s) and VMs ({2}s) can take {3}s together. Raise the shutdown time-out in Disk Settings.
timeouts_container: These containers ask for more time to stop than Unraid gives them ({1}s in Docker Settings): {0}
unclean: The last shutdown was not clean. The next array start runs a parity check.
share_open: {2} has {3} file(s) open on the share {1} over {0}.
share_writing: {2} is writing {3} file(s) to the share {1} over {0}, maybe a copy.
shares_ok: No open files on SMB or NFS shares.
ups_ok: The UPS is on mains power, battery at {0}%.
ups_battery: The UPS runs on battery: {0}% left, about {1} minutes.
ups_low: The UPS battery is almost empty: {0}% left, about {1} minutes.
flash_backup_ok: The last flash backup ({1}) is {0} day(s) old.
flash_backup_old: The last flash backup ({1}) is {0} days old. Back up the flash before rebooting.
flash_backup_none: FireSquire knows of no flash backup. BombVault in your fortress or Unraid Connect can keep one.
flash_backup_none_connect: FireSquire knows of no flash backup. Unraid Connect can keep one.
f_lead: In your fortress, FireSquire asks your other apps before a reboot whether one of them is still at work, and BombVault tells it when the flash drive was last backed up.
f_join_info: Enter your fortress phrase, the twelve words. FireSquire joins as soon as all twelve are in, and it keeps only its own keys, never the phrase.
f_err_phrase: Those words are not a fortress phrase. Please check each one once more.
f_err_member: FireSquire is in a fortress already.
f_err_not_member: FireSquire is not in a fortress.
f_nohelper: The fortress helper is not installed yet, so FireSquire cannot join a fortress for now.
f_none: No other app has joined your fortress yet.
f_leave_body: Your other apps will not see FireSquire anymore, and the check goes on without them. The phrase brings FireSquire back any time.
flash_probe_left: FireSquire could not delete its test file {0} on the flash. Please delete it yourself.
